headline: Benchmark firm Artificial Analysis released a test in which leading AI models write code to control a robotic arm, and OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra came first with a score of 69.
score_reason: Pool score 5 lowered by 1: released on 14 Oct 2026, a small preview test reported secondhand.
importance_line: Robot makers and researchers learn that general AI models can run a simple arm but are about 100 times slower than people, though the test is a small research preview of 8 tasks on one arm.
summary: Robot Forward Outlook, republished by 36Kr, reports that Artificial Analysis, a US AI benchmark company, tested five models on eight desktop tasks such as pressing a button and placing objects with a robotic arm, and that GPT-6 Astra averaged about 30 minutes and $16.36 per task, close to 100 times slower than a human. Artificial Analysis calls the release a research preview and the report notes that the models often struggled to tell when a task was finished.
notes: Full text from fulltext file; original Artificial Analysis release not read.
